podcast.title: Declaration at Final Bauhaus Gig
podcast.body: At the conclusion of Bauhaus's final gig at the Hammersmith Palais on July 5, 1983, David J famously grabbed the microphone and declared, "rest in peace," signifying the band's official end. "As the gig at the Hammersmith Pele came to an end, David J grabbed the mic and said, rest in peace."

podcast.title: Name Preference - David J
podcast.body: Although his full name is David John Haskins, he prefers to be addressed by the initial of his middle name, "David J." "although we know David by the initial of his middle name, John, he prefers to be called David J."

podcast.title: Post-Bauhaus Solo and The Sinister Ducks
podcast.body: After the splintering of Bauhaus in 1983, David J initially pursued a solo career before forming a group called The Sinister Ducks, which, however, did not last for a significant period. "at first, he went solo, too. Then he formed a group called The Sinister Ducks, but they didn't last very long."

podcast.title: Producing and Joining The Jazz Butcher
podcast.body: David J was invited to produce an album for the group The Jazz Butcher. He found the experience so enjoyable that he subsequently joined the band as a member for a period. "Then he was invited to produce an album for a group called The Jazz Butcher, and he enjoyed the experience so much that he actually ended up joining the band for a while."

xref.title: Band Breakup - Hammersmith Palais (1983)
xref.body: Bauhaus concluded their initial run with a final performance on July 5, 1983, at the Hammersmith Palais in London. The breakup was attributed to rising egos, creative differences, the pressures of touring, and Peter Murphy's severe bout of pneumonia, which forced the band to record an album without him, leading to internal divisions. "As the gig at the Hammersmith Pele came to an end, David J grabbed the mic and said, rest in peace. And that was that. Bajaos was dead."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Commercial Success - Beyond Bauhaus
xref.body: Love and Rockets achieved greater commercial success than Bauhaus, selling millions of records globally, headlining large tours, and securing a Top 40 hit in America. "As Love in Rockets, Daniel Ash, David J and Kevin Haskins were far more successful than Bajaos could have ever been, selling millions of records around the world, playing huge headlined tours and even having a top 40 hit in America."

xref.title: Final Performance
xref.body: Bauhaus's final gig on July 5, 1983, took place at the Hammersmith Palais in London, where David J famously grabbed the microphone at the end of the show and declared, "rest in peace," signaling the band's demise. "It was one final gig. July 5th, 1983, at the Hammersmith Pele in London."

xref.title: Post-Bauhaus Success
xref.body: Formed by Daniel Ash, David J, and Kevin Haskins after Peter Murphy declined a Bauhaus reunion, Love and Rockets achieved greater commercial success than Bauhaus. They sold millions of records worldwide, headlined large tours, and secured a Top 40 hit in America. "Daniel Ash, David J and Kevin Haskins were far more successful than Bajaos could have ever been selling millions of records around the world, playing huge headline tours, and even having a top 40 hit in America."

xref.title: Post-Breakup Projects
xref.body: After the band Bauhaus "splintered," its members went on to form other significant groups, including Tones on Tail and Love and Rockets. Additionally, the individual members, Peter Murphy, David J, and Daniel Ash, pursued solo careers. "Bauhaus splintered into tones on tail and loving rockets and indirectly gave us Peter Murphy, David J and Daniel Ash."
